post_brief.opening_direction: Start with the practical tension behind hybrid work policies.
post_brief.pattern_interrupt: The policy document matters less than the operating habits it creates.
post_brief.core_point: Hybrid work needs clear expectations, inclusive norms, and active attention to isolation.

evidence_to_use.evidence_text: A remote work policy should define expectations, communication norms, and responsibilities so distributed teams can work with fewer misunderstandings.
Inclusive workplace guidance treats diversity broadly, including race, gender, age, sexual orientation, and socioeconomic status.
Research on the long-term shift to remote work highlights increased feelings of isolation, especially for people living alone.

post_brief.practical_point: Make hybrid policy a living operating system, not a static document.
post_brief.ending_direction: Close by tying clarity, inclusion, and isolation into one leadership responsibility.
post_brief.cta_direction: Ask what hybrid teams should clarify first.

angle_decision.controlling_angle: Hybrid policies only work when they connect operational clarity with human support.
angle_decision.reader_problem: Leaders often write remote work rules without addressing the habits and support systems that make the rules usable.
angle_decision.author_position: Treat hybrid policy as a leadership system for clarity, inclusion, and isolation risk.
angle_decision.main_tension: A policy can look complete while still leaving people unclear, excluded, or isolated.
angle_decision.angle_to_avoid: Do not frame hybrid work as a generic flexibility perk.
